title: Building on the 5Cs: Digital Curation of Open Source Resources for Digital Health Innovation
content: Digital Health Innovation is by nature highly interdisciplinary and attracts people from a myriad of disciplines. These researchers often want to rapidly upskill but little time to find, judge and organise learning materials that are scattered across many organisations. This study utilises the 5Cs methodology to create a library of free educational resources for learners to develop knowledge and skills in digital health innovation. After examining the benefits and limitations of this methodology, we applied 4 of the 5 phases. Conceptualisation, the linking together of disparate artifacts to make new understandings of the content, was not applicable in this context. To evaluate the effectiveness of this free library, nine participants were interviewed and a thematic analysis of their responses conducted. Learners valued the assurance resources in the library had been selected and judged by a trusted source, but a lack of time and lack of communication limited use of the library. The 5Cs offers an effective methodology for curating open-source resources, with 4 of the 5Cs being applicable in this context.
